transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-22
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Rodriguez (ZenHealth - Head of Platform), Ethan Wu (ZenHealth - SRE), Lina Park (ZenHealth - Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick renewal check-in and expansion scoping. Customer interested in adding dedicated capacity in us-west-2 and eu-west-1, options for committed discounts, and alignment on security docs for procurement.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll run about 30, 40 minutes here. Quick intros - Alex from Redwood, Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:10] Maya Rodriguez: Hi, Maya here, thanks. Ethan and Lina with me.
[00:15] Priya Nair: Hi all. Quick agenda - renewal terms, capacity bump, regions, security checklist, and next steps. Sound good?
[00:25] Ethan Wu: Yep that works.
[01:05] Alex Chen: Cool. So, high level - you folks are up for renewal in about six weeks, is that right, Maya? I have the date as 2025-10-31 in our system.
[01:15] Maya Rodriguez: That's correct, end of October. We're looking at two things: one, extend the contract for another 12 months, and two, increase our committed capacity - traffic has grown a lot Q3.
[01:30] Alex Chen: Understood. Do you have a target uplift in mind? percentage or absolute GPU hours?
[01:42] Maya Rodriguez: We're looking at roughly 2.5x our current throughput. Right now we're on the hosted plan with occasional bursts to Dedicated; we'd like to move more steady-state traffic to Dedicated reserved capacity for cost predictability.
[01:55] Priya Nair: Makes sense. When you say 2.5x, is that sustained peak or average? That helps pick the right pool size and autoscale policy.
[02:10] Ethan Wu: That's sustained daytime traffic - average token volume has been up ~2.3x. Peaks are higher but short. We care about p95 latency staying under 220ms for our chat endpoints.
[02:22] Priya Nair: Got it. p95 220ms target. For that we usually recommend a mix: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 for most traffic and a second smaller Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 as a secondary region, plus prefix KV cache to reduce cold-starts.
[02:40] Maya Rodriguez: Yeah, ops prefers us-west for our West Coast users, and legal wants EU coverage in the next quarter - eu-west-1.
[02:50] Alex Chen: We can do a multi-region Dedicated footprint. Pricing note: adding regions incurs additional reserved capacity commitments, but we can model a blended committed discount. I'll put that in the quote.
[03:05] Lina Park: On procurement, we need an explicit clause about data residency and audit logs. Also, SOC2 attestation - do you have the latest report?
[03:15] Alex Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II - I'll attach the report and our security and compliance pack. For audit logs, Redwood Console supports per-route audit logs and export; we also have KMS integration details in the docs.
[03:30] Ethan Wu: Quick question, KMS - do you integrate with customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM? We need to ensure tokens and logs can be encrypted under our key.
[03:40] Priya Nair: Yes, customer-managed keys via KMS are supported for stored artifacts and at-rest model cache. On the runtime side, secrets used for the control plane are wrapped - there's some nuance for HSM but we can share the architecture doc.
[03:55] Maya Rodriguez: Awesome, please send those. For the renewal term length, we like 12 months, but we'd consider 24 months if the committed discount is meaningful. What's the typical uplift for a 2-year versus 1-year?
[04:10] Alex Chen: Typically the larger the commit and longer the term, the better discount. For example, a 12-month 2.5x commit might be X% off list, a 24-month could be an additional few percent - I'll quantify in the quote.
[04:25] Lina Park: We also need to know cancellation and early termination terms - procurement will want clear exit language.
[04:32] Alex Chen: Sure, standard enterprise terms, plus we can include a rolling downgrade path with pro-rated credits - I'll include the language in the draft SOW.
[04:45] Ethan Wu: On the technical side, Priya, we want to run a benchmark: simulate our workload in us-west-2 with our model variant (8-bit quantized) and our typical prompt mix. Can Redwood run that or do we run it ourselves?
[04:58] Priya Nair: We can run it on our staging Dedicated cluster in us-west-2, with your sample prompts if you share them. We'll capture KV cache hit rates, latency p50/p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:10] Maya Rodriguez: That would be perfect. We'd like the logs for procurement and to validate performance before committing.
[05:18] Priya Nair: Ok, action: we'll run a 48-hour benchmark at realistic traffic levels and share the perf dashboard and raw logs.
[05:25] Alex Chen: I'll add that as a contingent item in the quote - if the benchmark meets targets we'll finalize committed capacity.
[05:35] Maya Rodriguez: One more question on fallbacks - if Dedicated capacity is saturated, do you provide automatic fallback to hosted variants or other models to keep latency stable?
[05:46] Priya Nair: Yes, Smart Routing allows fallbacks by policy: region, model family, or cost-tier. We can configure canary ratios and automatic failover to reduce errors and degrade gracefully. Note, fallback to hosted may have slightly different token pricing.
[06:05] Ethan Wu: Good. Also, regarding KV cache - we rely heavily on prefix caching, how is that handled across regions? Is KV cache replicated or per-region?
[06:16] Priya Nair: KV cache is per-cluster for low-latency access; cross-region replication is available as an extra; otherwise you'd see lower cache hits for cold regions. If you need high hit rates in both EU and US, we recommend regional caches with warm-up policies.
[06:35] Maya Rodriguez: Okay. For the expansion timeline, we want eu-west-1 by EOY. Is that doable?
[06:42] Alex Chen: Yes, doable. We'd plan capacity procurement and provisioning - typically 2-4 weeks to stand up Dedicated in a new region once contract is signed, depending on exact instance types.
[07:00] Lina Park: Procurement question: Do we need a separate SOW for each region, or can it be a single SOW listing multiple regions?
[07:07] Alex Chen: Single SOW is fine with region-specific capacity line items; that makes billing and renewals simpler.
[07:18] Maya Rodriguez: Perfect.
[07:25] Priya Nair: Quick technical aside - Ethan, for your p95 220ms target, are you measuring from user request to first token or full-emit? That changes where we tune.
[07:36] Ethan Wu: We measure first-token latency end-to-end.
[07:39] Priya Nair: Ok, then to meet that you'll want lower batch windows and reserved GPU warm pools; we'll configure lower batching for chat endpoints and enable continuous KV cache warming. That affects cost a bit, we'll show trade-offs in the quote.
[07:55] Maya Rodriguez: Sounds reasonable. Can you show the cost delta between aggressive latency SLO and more cost-optimized profile?
[08:02] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll provide a cost matrix: latency-driven config vs cost-driven, plus the committed discount tiers for 12 vs 24 months.
[08:10] Lina Park: On legal paperwork, we need sample PO language and whether Redwood requires net-30 or net-45 - we prefer net-45.
[08:18] Alex Chen: Net-45 is standard for larger customers; we'll note that. PO language and invoice examples I'll include.
[08:25] Maya Rodriguez: Great. Any blockers for us to sign sooner?
[08:30] Alex Chen: The main items are: benchmark meeting your perf SLO, procurement sign-off on the quote, and SOC2/security docs. We'll send the draft quote and security pack today.
[08:39] Maya Rodriguez: Cool. Quick note: we ran into a subtle perf regression last month on the kv caching with your prior runtime - it was mentioned in the support ticket. Have those patches been rolled out?
[08:50] Priya Nair: Yes, the KV cache regression was addressed in runtime v1.8.2; we deployed mitigations and we'll include the release notes. If you still see edge cases we'll open a support P0.
[09:05] Ethan Wu: Thanks. Also, are there any self-serve UI features in the Console for capacity scaling we can use or is it all through Redwood ops?
[09:15] Alex Chen: For Dedicated, customers can self-serve minor autoscale policies and burst rules in the Console; provisioning new Dedicated pools or reserved capacity changes typically go through our sales ops to avoid accidental over-provisioning.
[09:30] Lina Park: Ok procurement prefers to minimize manual ops changes.
[09:36] Alex Chen: We'll lock down RBAC for your team so only approved users can change scaling policies.
[09:44] Maya Rodriguez: Good. Anything else on expansion?
[09:48] Priya Nair: One more thought: we can pre-warm model variants in eu-west-1 a few days before cutover to improve cache hit rate. There's a small one-time cost for pre-warm. We'll include that option.
[10:02] Maya Rodriguez: Let's include it as optional.
[10:07] Alex Chen: Ok. To recap next actions - I'll send updated quote (regions + 12 vs 24 mo scenarios), SOC2 + security pack, and sample SOW/PO language. Priya will run the benchmark and share logs. Lina will confirm procurement timeline. We'll reconvene after benchmark results.
[10:24] Maya Rodriguez: Yep. Thanks everyone.

Crosstalk / small talk for a bit...

[11:15] Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials today.
[11:20] (call ends)
